earlier_scan.source_named: Collins, James T. 2006. The Malayic variants of eastern Borneo. In Schulze & Warnk (eds.), Insular Southeast Asia. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz, 37-51.
earlier_scan.note: Dialectological chapter covering Berau Malay phonology (gemination, 3-vowel system); not online; stress statement unverified

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Berau Malay language'; Wikipedia (id) 'Bahasa Berau'; Wikipedia (ms) 'Bahasa Melayu Berau' (read 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. en: 3-vowel inventory /a i u/, loss of *h *ʔ, contrastive gemination (tabu vs tabbu, ini vs inni), sourced to Collins 2006. id: only vowels a i u, loan e>i o>u, h dropped.

sources.citation: Mayangsari, Dewi; Inderajati, Aal. 2023. Leksikostatistik dan Glotokronologi Bahasa Berau dengan Bahasa Minangkabau. Widyaparwa 51(2): 377-391. DOI 10.26499/wdprw.v51i2.1410.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. 200-item Swadesh comparison with phonemic correspondence sets (e.g. Berau final-syllable /t/, /s/ correspondences); no suprasegmental remarks. Its bibliography led to Febianti 2017 and Kurniawati et al. 2002.

sources.citation: Zahara, Hikmah Nur; Indrahastuti, Tri; Elyana, Kukuh. 2023. Analisis Bentuk dan Makna Kata Berafiks yang Berkategori Verbal pada Bahasa Berau. Adjektiva: Educational Languages and Literature Studies 6(1): 34-45. DOI 10.30872/adjektiva.v6i1.2113.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Verbal affixation and morphophonemics only (prefixes ba-, ma-/man-/mang-/many-, ta-; suffixes -kan, -i); remarks that Berau lacks the letters e, o, f, v, q, z. No mention of tekanan/aksen.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (revised ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics. [held by the project at]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Berau Malay only once (ch. 4, p. 230): 'Medial geminates are also found in some of the non-standard Malay dialects of Borneo, as in Berau Malay (Collins 1992).' Nothing on Berau stress.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1994. Preliminary notes on Berau Malay. In Peter W. Martin (ed.), Shifting Patterns of Language Use in Borneo (Borneo Research Council Proceedings Series 3), 297-333. Williamsburg, VA: Borneo Research Council.

sources.note: The only descriptive sketch of Berau Malay in Glottolog (37 pp.); Collins' dialect notes normally include a phonology section with segment inventory, gemination and accent remarks — the most likely locus of a first-hand stress statement.
